Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted routing, VPC deployment, and KV/prefix caching. Agreed next steps: updated quote, SOC2 docs, and targeted benchmark next week.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-22
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Park (Redwood SE), Daniel Ruiz (Helios - Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Helios - SRE), Amir Khan (Helios - Security)

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, quick agenda: renewal terms, expansion - additional EU region, and the capacity bump you mentioned. Leo will cover perf and the benchmark plan.
00:12 Daniel Ruiz: Yep thanks Maya, appreciate it. We just want to make sure the numbers and timeline align with our Q3 launch.
00:18 Maya Chen: Totally, quick check - current contract ends 2026-09-30 right?
00:21 Daniel Ruiz: Correct, and we're looking to extend and put new reserved capacity in place by early July if possible.
00:29 Leo Park: Quick note, on the perf side we ran the 95th/99th pct tests last month, but we can tighten them to match the production seq length distribution you sent.
00:38 Priya Nair: We emailed the logs and a sample traffic profile. Most requests are 128 to 512 tokens, some spikes to 1k for report generation.
00:47 Leo Park: Great that's perfect. For the cost/latency tradeoff, if you go 2x reserved capacity we can keep 99th pct latency under 350ms for typical chat flows, with some quantization on the model variant.
01:02 Amir Khan: Can you clarify what you mean by quantization here - does it impact accuracy or require a different model?
01:08 Leo Park: Good question. We have Redwood-verified quant profiles; most workloads see negligible quality regression for int8 on the decoder-only stack. For the long-form report bits we can route those to a higher-precision flavor.
01:23 Daniel Ruiz: OK, so split routing by route, low-latency chat on quantized variants, heavyweight reports to full fp16. Does Redwood support automatic fallback if capacity is hit?
01:34 Maya Chen: Yes, we have smart routing - policy-based. You can set a primary in us-west and fallback to the EU or a hosted burst pool. For enterprise we recommend dedicated + regional pins so data residency is respected.
01:47 Priya Nair: We need EU region since customers in EEA require data residency. Is that an add-on or included in the reserved contract?
01:56 Maya Chen: It's an add-on region. For the quote we'll include EU-west as an extra line item. If you commit to annual reserved capacity we can credit some setup fees.
02:10 Daniel Ruiz: Timeline wise, how quickly can EU capacity be provisioned?
02:14 Leo Park: Typically 2-3 weeks from signed amendment - provisioning and testing. If you need on-prem or VPC private plane that's a bit longer - say 4-6 weeks.
02:25 Amir Khan: VPC private control plane - we need to confirm encryption at rest with our KMS and audit log retention. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
02:34 Maya Chen: Yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping. We'll table the SOC2 & ISO artifacts for you.
02:44 Amir Khan: Also what about RBAC and SSO? We need SAML enterprise SSO and role-based access - no shared accounts.
02:52 Leo Park: We support SAML SSO + granular RBAC. We'll send the role mapping doc. Sometimes the auto-transcription of roles in our older docs calls it 'role mapping' but it's the same.
03:05 Priya Nair: On the performance side, when you say 2x reserved, do you mean double GPUs or double throughput? We want predictable TPS not just headroom.
03:15 Maya Chen: Good call - by 2x reserved we mean reserved vGPU capacity that maps to expected throughput. We'll size it to your 1k rps p95 target based on the traffic mix you shared.
03:27 Leo Park: I'll run a targeted benchmark: 1k rps sustained with the mixed profile (128-1k tokens). I'll also measure 99th percentile tail and upstream latency when your app sits behind our routing.
03:39 Daniel Ruiz: Any chance of running a third-party latency test? Our infra team likes to see independent results.
03:45 Leo Park: Yep we can coordinate - we have a benchmark harness and can export logs for your third-party. We can also run a canary in the EU region after provisioning.
03:55 Priya Nair: About caching - we use a lot of prefix reuse in the assistant. How does Redwood's prefix/KV cache work? We want to avoid repeated compute for similar prompts.
04:06 Leo Park: We have automatic KV and prefix caching at the serving runtime; it's workload-aware. Small caveat: cache warm-up can produce slightly higher latency until hot prefixes stabilize. But for high reuse you'll see big cost wins.
04:20 Daniel Ruiz: Are those cache metrics visible in the console? We need token-level cost breakdown by route.
04:25 Maya Chen: Yes, Console shows per-route token counts, cache hits, and cost breakdown. We'll include dashboard screenshots in the notes.
04:36 Amir Khan: Security: retention SLAs - can you set different retention periods per route? For example, EU PII requests need 30 day retention, dev logs 7 days.
04:46 Maya Chen: We can set retention at the workspace level and override per-route via policies; I'll confirm exact limits.
04:53 Amir Khan: Also need audit log export to our SIEM.
04:57 Leo Park: We support streaming audit logs to your SIEM and can provide S3 export for long-term retention.
05:06 Daniel Ruiz: OK - circling back to pricing. If we go 2x reserved and add EU region what kind of delta over our current spend?
05:14 Maya Chen: Ballpark with the model mix you have, expect ~1.9-2.3x current hosted spend if fully reserved with EU. Exact quote coming shortly.
05:23 Daniel Ruiz: That is in range. We'll probably extend for 12 months and do a mid-year capacity review.
05:29 Maya Chen: Sounds good - for the renewal we'll prepare an amendment with the EU region line, 2x reserved GPUs, and the support tier you already have.
05:36 Priya Nair: Any gotchas for migration? We have some probes that assume certain response times and might need threshold adjustments during rollouts.
05:44 Leo Park: We'll provide traffic shaping guidance and a canary plan. Also recommend gradual rollout per region and automatic fallback to hosted pool for safety.
05:54 Daniel Ruiz: Great. Let's capture next steps.
05:58 Maya Chen: Next steps: Maya will send updated quote and amendment by 6/24; Leo will schedule and run the benchmark week of 6/29 and share logs; Amir will compile compliance artifact list and retention requirements by 6/25. Anything else?
06:15 Amir Khan: We'll also want a quick follow-up call after the benchmark to review tail latency.
06:20 Maya Chen: Perfect - I'll schedule a 30-minute follow up the week after the benchmark. Thanks all.
06:26 Daniel Ruiz: Thanks everyone, appreciate it.
06:29 End of recording

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-heard acronyms (e.g., kayvee cache for KV cache) and occasional speaker label flips in the auto transcript. Shared artifacts: quote draft (link: drive.redwood/quotes/CRM-389021), SOC2 pack (link: drive.redwood/compliance/SOC2), perf harness notes (link: drive.redwood/benchmarks/helios).
